Action items we covered:

- Rishi will confirm default retention windows and the options for disabling storage on hosted vs Dedicated/Private.

Neha — thanks for the recap and the materials, looks great. A couple quick clarifying questions from our security review before we schedule the follow-up session:

1) For hosted API customers, does Redwood persist full request payloads and the model outputs by default? If so, what is the default retention window and is the stored data encrypted at rest with customer-specific keys?
2) Can we choose a retention policy of zero days (no persistence) for certain routes/keys? We want to avoid storing PHI for a subset of API calls.
3) For Dedicated/Private deployments, does any customer data leave our VPC/region? We need explicit confirmation that for Private deployments we can keep everything in our account/region.

Also: for a security review artifact, could you provide a single-paragraph statement we can paste into our internal approval ticket that summarizes custody/retention behavior for prompts and generated outputs?

Sarah
Sarah Jensen
Head of Platform Security | MedTech Inc.
sarah.jensen@medtechinc.com

Hi Sarah — Rishi from Product Security here, following up with concrete answers and options. Short answers up front, followed by specifics you can paste into your ticket.

Short answers:
- Hosted API default behavior: We persist full request payloads (inputs) and model outputs for up to 30 days by default to support debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. These artifacts are encrypted at rest using AWS KMS; per-tenant keying is available on enterprise plans.
- Opt-out/zero-persistence: Yes — customers on Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private deployments can configure no-persistence for inference payloads and outputs. For hosted API customers we offer an enterprise opt-out that disables storage for selected API keys/routes and replaces persistence with ephemeral-only routing (contact your AE to enable).
- Data residency: For hosted customers, logs and stored artifacts remain in the region you select (we currently support us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). Private deployments keep all data within your VPC and never transit Redwood-managed object stores.

Pluggable details (pasteable paragraph):
"Redwood Inference persists request and response artifacts for hosted API customers for a default retention window of 30 days; aggregated telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are retained for 90 days. Stored artifacts are encrypted at rest with AWS KMS; tenant-specific keys are available for enterprise contracts. Customers requiring zero-persistence may opt into route-level no-persistence on Dedicated or Private deployments, and enterprise hosted customers can request an opt-out for specific API keys which routes inference through an ephemeral-only path. Private deployments do not send data to Redwood-managed object stores and remain inside the customer VPC/region. Deletion-on-request and audit logging are available under our DPA and SLA terms."

Additional controls we can offer on request:
- Per-route ingestion filters (strip or redact PII before any persistence)
- Prompt hashing + token-level redaction before storage
- Automatic KV-cache eviction for long-context jobs so caches are not serialized to long-term stores

I'll attach the custody statement Neha referenced and a short FAQ for the security review. Happy to jump on a call with your team to walk through KMS setup and deletion workflow.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
